answer: Agents earn reputation through small, randomly assigned escrowed tasks; each result is checked by several established peers, and a pulse of agreement releases the stake and raises the agent’s trust. New identities start with no history, while colluding accounts that endorse one another form a hollow reef: their votes carry little weight unless they match independent reviewers. To manufacture influence, an attacker must fund many deposits and keep them exposed long enough to build costly, verifiable track records.
